126228.overview: Another game from the Time & Fun series. This is the French release by Ludotronic.

126250.overview: Zeke Wolf must catch chicken eggs rolling down four chutes. Each egg gives the player one point, and if the player can get 200 and 500 points, all misses are erased. As the game progresses, the eggs will slide down faster. The player uses four separate buttons to move the wolf between the catching positions.

129202.overview:
Moles pop out of the ground, attempting to get into the player's garden. To keep them away, the player must move left and right and smack them with hammers. As the game progresses, the moles will move faster. If any moles are left untouched for a few seconds, the player gets penalized with a miss. The player receives a Game Over when they have three misses.

Misses cannot be cleared at all in this Game & Watch title, which means the player needs to be very cautious.

190478.overview: You are a treasure hunter seeking the treasure hidden in a coffin in Dracula's castle. But watch out — dangers lie ahead! You must escape the Wolfman, break down a wall to enter the Underground Labyrinth and evade a Vampire Bat as you try to collect all the diamonds. In Dracula's Castle, there are four coffins. Chose carefully — only one coffin contains the treasure. If you open the wrong one, you'll find Dracula inside instead of the treasure.

190483.overview:
The Electronic Quarterback is a handheld electronic sports game released by Coleco in 1978. Famous for its bright red LED "blips" representing players, it became a pop-culture staple of the era and even appeared in the 1982 movie TRON.

Players control the quarterback "blip" to pass, kick, or run past the defensive "blips" controlled by the computer.

477452.overview:
Are you a professional bowler? Then challenge your friends to a game of Tiger Bowling!
Player selection: The PLAYER button allows you to choose between single-player mode (Player 1) or two-player challenge mode (Player 2) alternately.
Game Frames: The game consists of 10 complete frames, just like the rules of real bowling.
The player's cartoon character moves on screen in preparation for throwing the ball, and the secret of the game lies in the timing of pressing the button during the player's arm movement.
